captions.detailed: A 3D-printable thumbwheel featuring a wide, flat cylindrical base with a highly textured, serrated outer edge containing small triangular ridges. A raised, thick-walled cylindrical boss sits in the center of the wheel. This central boss features a hexagonal socket extending all the way through, designed to hold a nut or hex bolt head securely.
captions.instruction: Please design a parametric thumbwheel in OpenSCAD with a finely serrated outer grip and a central raised boss containing a hexagonal nut pocket. The script should allow customization of the wheel diameter, wheel depth, nut depth, nut corner-to-corner diameter, and the wall thickness surrounding the nut.
captions.factory: The script imports the MCAD/regular_shapes library. It uses a difference() operation to subtract a linear-extruded hexagon (representing the nut socket) from a union of two parts: a main wheel and a central cylindrical boss. The main wheel is constructed by linear-extruding a series of rotated triangles generated in a for-loop to create the serrated outer grip, while the central boss is a simple cylinder with a radius defined by the nut radius plus the wall thickness.
